item.question: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm. Is it an isosceles triangle? Fold it in half and say what you notice about its angles.
steps: Compare the sides: 5 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm. Two sides are equal (5 cm and 5 cm) and the third side is different (3 cm).
A triangle with 2 equal sides is an isosceles triangle, so this is an isosceles triangle.
Fold it in half through the corner where the two 5 cm sides meet, so that the two 5 cm sides lie on each other.
The two halves match exactly. The two corners at the ends of the 3 cm side land on each other.
So the two angles at the ends of the 3 cm side are equal.
Check: the fold splits the triangle into two halves that match, so equal sides and equal angles come as a pair.
item.answer: Yes, it is an isosceles triangle: it has 2 equal sides (5 cm and 5 cm). When it is folded in half the two halves match, so it also has 2 equal angles
item.text:
Worked example: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm. Is it an isosceles triangle? Fold it in half and say what you notice about its angles.

2. A triangle with 2 equal sides is an isosceles triangle, so this is an isosceles triangle.
3. Fold it in half through the corner where the two 5 cm sides meet, so that the two 5 cm sides lie on each other.
4. The two halves match exactly. The two corners at the ends of the 3 cm side land on each other.
5. So the two angles at the ends of the 3 cm side are equal.
6. Check: the fold splits the triangle into two halves that match, so equal sides and equal angles come as a pair.
Answer: Yes, it is an isosceles triangle: it has 2 equal sides (5 cm and 5 cm). When it is folded in half the two halves match, so it also has 2 equal angles

item.question: Triangle A has sides 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. Triangle B has sides 7 cm, 5 cm and 4 cm. Triangle C has sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 3 cm. Name each triangle and say how many of its angles are equal.
steps: Triangle A: the sides are 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. All 3 sides are equal, so A is an equilateral triangle.
Fold A in half through a corner, so that the two halves lie on each other. They match through every corner, so all 3 angles of A are equal.
Triangle B: the sides are 7 cm, 5 cm and 4 cm. No two sides are equal, so B is a scalene triangle.
Fold B in half through each of its corners. The two halves never lie exactly on each other, so no two angles of B are equal.
Triangle C: the sides are 8 cm, 8 cm and 3 cm. Two sides are equal, so C is an isosceles triangle with 2 equal angles.
Check: A has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles, C has 2 and 2, and B has none and none. The number of equal sides and the number of equal angles always match.
item.answer: A is equilateral (3 equal sides, 3 equal angles), B is scalene (no equal sides, no equal angles), C is isosceles (2 equal sides, 2 equal angles)

steps_tex: Each piece is a triangle with $1$ right angle and $3$ different sides: a shortest side, a middle side and a longest side. The longest side is twice the shortest side.
Join $2$ pieces side to side. They can meet along their shortest sides, their middle sides or their longest sides, and the second piece can be flipped over or turned half way round.
Along the middle sides, with one piece flipped over: a triangle with all $3$ sides equal.
Along the shortest sides, with one piece flipped over: a wider triangle with $2$ equal sides.
Along the longest sides, with one piece flipped over: a kite. With one piece turned half way round: a rectangle.
Along the middle sides or along the shortest sides, with one piece turned half way round: $2$ different parallelograms that are not rectangles.
Check: $2$ triangles and $4$ four-sided shapes make $2 + 4 = 6$ shapes, and each one has $3$ or $4$ sides.

item.question: Is it possible to make a triangle where all three sides are equal (equilateral triangle)?
steps_tex: We want a triangle with $3$ sides of the same length.
Join $2$ pieces along their middle sides, with one piece flipped over.
The longest sides of the $2$ pieces become $2$ sides of the new triangle. They are equal.
The $2$ shortest sides of the pieces lie in one straight line and make the third side. The shortest side is half the longest side, so $2$ shortest sides are as long as $1$ longest side.
So all $3$ sides are equal: an equilateral triangle.
Check: measure the $3$ sides with a ruler. They are the same.
item.answer_tex: Yes. Join $2$ pieces along their middle sides, with one piece flipped over. All $3$ sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle.

item.question: Is it possible to make a triangle where all three sides are unequal?
steps_tex: One piece is already a triangle. Its $3$ sides are a shortest side, a middle side and a longest side, and they are all different.
So a single piece is a triangle with all $3$ sides unequal.

Bigger ones are possible too. Join the wider triangle ($2$ pieces) and $1$ more piece, longest side against one of the $2$ equal sides, and flip the piece until the outside has only $3$ sides. The $3$ sides are all different.
A triangle with all $3$ sides unequal is called a scalene triangle.
Check: a single piece has $3$ different sides, so the answer is yes.
item.answer_tex: Yes. A single piece has $3$ different sides, and $3$ pieces can also make a bigger triangle with $3$ different sides. It is a scalene triangle.

item.question: Take an equilateral triangle. Check if all the angles of an equilateral triangle are equal, just like you did with the isosceles triangle.
steps_tex: An equilateral triangle has $3$ equal sides.
Fold it in half through one corner, so that the $2$ sides at that corner lie on each other.
The two halves match exactly, so the other $2$ corners land on each other and those $2$ angles are equal.
Fold again through a different corner. The two halves match again, so another pair of angles is equal.
Every pair of the $3$ corners matches, so all $3$ angles are equal.
Check: $3$ equal sides go with $3$ equal angles.
item.answer_tex: Yes. The two halves match when folded through every corner, so all $3$ angles of an equilateral triangle are equal.

item.question: Now, cut the equilateral triangle in half. How many sides of each new triangle are equal?
steps_tex: Cut the equilateral triangle along a line from one corner to the middle of the opposite side. Each half is a triangle.
Look at the $3$ sides of one half: half of an old side, the cut line, and a whole old side.
The cut line is longer than half of an old side and shorter than a whole old side. So the $3$ sides are all different.
No side of the new triangle is equal to another side.
Check: each half has the same shape as a piece of the rhombus, with a shortest side, a middle side and a longest side.

item.question: Check in scalene triangles whether any two or more angles are equal?
steps_tex: Take a scalene triangle, for example one piece of the rhombus. Its $3$ sides are all different.
Try to fold it so that the two halves match. Try with each corner.
The halves never match, so no $2$ angles are equal.
One angle is a right angle. The other $2$ angles are smaller than a right angle, and they are different from each other.
Check: all $3$ sides different goes with all $3$ angles different.

item.question: A four-sided shape has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 3 cm and 3 cm going round in that order. Is it a kite? Then check a shape whose sides going round are 5 cm, 3 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm.
steps: Name the sides in order: side 1 is 5 cm, side 2 is 5 cm, side 3 is 3 cm and side 4 is 3 cm.
Side 1 and side 2 are next to each other and both are 5 cm, so side 1 = side 2. They are adjacent sides.
Side 3 and side 4 are next to each other and both are 3 cm, so side 3 = side 4.
Two pairs of adjacent sides are equal, so the shape is a kite.
Now the second shape: 5 cm, 3 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm. Side 1 and side 3 are both 5 cm, but they are opposite sides, not next to each other.
Side 2 and side 4 are both 3 cm and also opposite. Equal opposite sides make a parallelogram, so this shape is not a kite.
Check: both shapes have two 5 cm sides and two 3 cm sides. Only the order round the shape decides.
item.answer: The first shape is a kite, because its equal sides are next to each other (side 1 = side 2 and side 3 = side 4). The second shape has equal opposite sides, so it is a parallelogram, not a kite

item.question: A four-sided shape has sides 8 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm going round. What is it called? What more do we need to know to call it a rectangle?
steps: Look at the opposite sides: the first and third sides are 8 cm and 8 cm, and the second and fourth sides are 5 cm and 5 cm.
Opposite sides are equal, so the shape is a parallelogram.
In a parallelogram the opposite angles are equal.
Now look at the angles. If all 4 angles are right angles, the parallelogram is a rectangle.
A slanted shape with the same sides 8 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm has no right angle. It is a parallelogram that is not a rectangle.
Check: every rectangle is a parallelogram, but a parallelogram is a rectangle only when its angles are right angles.
item.answer: It is a parallelogram, because its opposite sides are equal. It is a rectangle only if all 4 angles are right angles; a slanted shape with the same sides is not a rectangle
